findings.title: `correct --context` silently drops the supplied context when the target is a declared continuous attribute
findings.evidence: Real CLI, fresh data dir: `clio persona observe pref.formality 0.5 --bank demo --actor agent` registered the continuous attribute; `clio correct pref.formality 0.7 --reason "recenter formality" --context "team chat" --bank demo --actor agent --output json` returned `{"ok":true,"rule":"continuous",...}` and wrote no context. The `correct` audit row is `{"as_of":...,"attr_key":"pref.formality","observed_value":0.7,"reason":"recenter formality","state":...,"trend":...}`; no audit row or item contains `team chat`. Code: `crates/clio-compliance/src/correct.rs:111-118` routes a declared attribute to `route_declared`, which never reads `args.context` (`crates/clio-compliance/src/correct.rs:121-152`); context validation only runs on the discrete path (`crates/clio-compliance/src/correct.rs:181-183`).
findings.requirement_ref: FR-34 (preserve through update/correct); phase Task 3/4 (no silent discard); phase file Known Limitations does not name this path
findings.recommendation: Reject a supplied `context` on the continuous route with a usage/domain error, or persist it on the continuous audit row; add a clio-compliance regression test for `correct` + `context` against a declared continuous attribute.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED by fail-closed rejection (the finding's first recommended option). `route_declared` now refuses a supplied `context` when the target's declared `update_rule` is Continuous: crates/clio-compliance/src/correct.rs:129-143 returns `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` with a message that names the route and never echoes the value; item-addressed corrections keep the documented replace/preserve semantics (correct.rs:72-77). Regression test: crates/clio-compliance/src/correct_context_tests.rs:154-231 `context_on_the_continuous_route_is_rejected_without_a_write` (asserts the error code, that the message does not contain the supplied value, that NO EMA observation is written (`continuous_series` stays empty), and that the same correction without `context` still re-centers the state). Real CLI, same data dir before/after: BEFORE (pre-fix binary) `clio correct pref.formality 0.7 --reason "recenter formality" --context "team chat" --bank demo --actor agent --output json` -> `{"ok":true,"rule":"continuous","state":{...}}` exit 0 (silent drop); AFTER the same command -> exit 1 `{"code":"invalid_argument","message":"attribute `pref.formality` is re-centered through its EMA state, which carries no item context; omit `context` for a continuous correction","ok":false}`; the same call WITHOUT `--context` -> exit 0 with the re-centered state; control: discrete `clio correct itm-cli-217060360-503662 "meeting at 5pm" --reason "moved again" --context "team chat"` -> exit 0 and `clio get itm-mcp-1` shows `context: "team chat"`. Test run: `cargo test -p clio-compliance --locked correct_context_tests` -> `test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 106 filtered out`.

findings.title: `inspect` now fails the whole listing when any listed item's sealed body cannot be decrypted for a non-erasure reason (legacy opaque rows)
findings.evidence: `crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs:216-237` calls `get_memory_item` per row and returns the error for anything except `ErasedSubject` (`:230-231`). `crates/clio-mcp/src/context_read_schema_tests.rs:120-138` (`inspect_propagates_non_erasure_content_errors`) asserts that one legacy `put_item` row makes the entire `inspect` call fail with `invalid_argument`. Before this change `inspect` was metadata-only (`git show HEAD:crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs` inspect used `inspect_items` only), so a bank containing such rows listed fine.
findings.requirement_ref: Phase Objective (existing items remain readable); AC-100601-05; Task 4
findings.recommendation: Treat an unreadable sealed body like the erased case: keep the metadata row and omit context for that row; restrict hard failure to genuine authorization errors, and update the test to assert the resilient behavior.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED by resilience. r1 kept a `Forbidden` hard-fail guard, which was WRONG: `clio-store`'s KMS maps AEAD authentication failure to `Forbidden` (crates/clio-store/src/dek.rs:307), so an undecryptable body still aborted the listing. r2 removed the guard entirely: crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs inspect's per-row enrichment is now `if let Ok(Some(item)) = ... { insert context }` — every per-row body failure (missing DEK, DEK version mismatch, AEAD authentication failure, crypto-shredded subject, legacy opaque row) keeps the metadata row and omits `context`, matching `clio_store::open_context` (audit views) and retrieval's unreadable-item skip (`clio-retrieve/src/hybrid.rs:395-401`). The doc comment now states the truth: the only caller authorization at that layer is the bank-scoped query; a direct `get` on the id still reports the underlying error. Regression test: crates/clio-mcp/src/context_read_schema_tests.rs:155-202 `inspect_survives_undecryptable_ciphertext_rows` opens a file-backed DB under key-store 1, reopens under a fresh key store 2 (same database) and mints a new DEK for one subject, so one row fails with `forbidden` "no DEK for subject" and another with `forbidden` "content decryption failed"; the test asserts `ok == true`, all 3 rows listed, all unreadable rows omit `context`. Reproduction with the real CLI on a copied data dir (one flipped character inside the stored `ciphertext_b64`, envelope still valid base64): BEFORE the fix `clio inspect --bank demo --actor agent --output json` -> exit 1 `{"code":"forbidden","message":"content decryption failed","ok":false}`; AFTER the same command -> exit 0, `ok:true`, the metadata row listed with `context` omitted; `clio get itm-cli-101460420-546948` on the same dir still exit 1 `forbidden` "content decryption failed" (direct read reports the row's own error, unchanged). Test run: `cargo test -p clio-mcp --locked` -> `test result: ok. 290 passed; 0 failed`. Remediation r3 corrected the two phase-file statements that still described the removed guard (`roadmap/phase-100601-native-source-context.md:531` evidence row and `:628` Known Limitations, current numbering): both now state that `inspect` performs its bank-scoped authorization before enrichment, retains the metadata row and omits `context` for every per-row body read failure with no per-row hard-fail guard, and leaves direct `get` error reporting unchanged, and the F-02 evidence row cites `inspect_survives_undecryptable_ciphertext_rows` (plus `inspect_survives_an_unreadable_legacy_row` and `inspect_survives_a_crypto_shredded_subject`). r3 re-verification on the current binary: `cargo test -p clio-mcp --locked inspect_survives` -> `3 passed; 0 failed`; fresh tampered copy (one flipped `ciphertext_b64` char) -> `clio inspect --bank demo --actor agent --output json` exit 0 `ok:true` with the metadata row kept and no `context` key, `clio get <id> --bank demo --actor agent --output json` exit 1 `forbidden` `content decryption failed`.

findings.title: Published `inspect` description and in-code doc still say the listing never returns payload/decrypted content, but it now returns decrypted `context`
findings.evidence: `crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_read_defs.rs:277-279` publishes "List items with epistemic_kind, scores, validity windows (never payloads/DEKs)." and `crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs:189` says "Never returns ciphertext, DEKs, or decrypted content". Both contradict `crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs:216-237` and the passing test `crates/clio-mcp/src/context_read_schema_tests.rs:64-79`, where `inspect` returns `"context":"inspect context"`.
findings.requirement_ref: Task 1 (update the tool catalog/schemas together); Task 3 (schemas describe the same behavior)
findings.recommendation: Update the published `inspect` description and the module doc to state that the listing includes optional source `context` as metadata for authorized readers.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED. crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_read_defs.rs:278 now publishes "List items with epistemic_kind, scores, validity windows, and optional source context for authorized readers (never payloads/DEKs)." and the `inspect` doc comment in crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs:187-194 matches the behaviour (metadata rows plus the optional decrypted `context` for readable items; never ciphertext/DEKs/payloads). Real evidence from the built CLI: `clio mcp schema-export` prints that exact `inspect` description (verified by parsing the exported tool pack). No schema shape, property, or limit changed.

findings.title: Phase-file Definition of Done claims "no-context paths byte-identical by test", but no-context audit telemetry changed and no test asserts byte identity
findings.evidence: `crates/clio-store/src/item_persist.rs:49-61` returns `{"context_present":false,"context_len":0}` for absent context, and `crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_memory.rs:208-222`, `crates/clio-store/src/postgres_memory.rs:173-186`, `crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs:124-133` now bind that as `detail_json` where `'{}'` was written before. Real CLI run: `clio remember "no context note" --category task_spec --bank demo --actor agent`, then the audit row is `create_memory_item | {"context_len":0,"context_present":false}`. The phase file DoD states "no-context paths byte-identical by test".
findings.recommendation: Scope the claim to the sealed payload (which `content_envelope` tests do pin) and state that audit telemetry is additively extended for every create/update/correct.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED by correcting the phase-file claim. The Definition-of-Done bullet now reads: "Existing behavior remains intact (regression suites green; the *sealed payload* of an item written without context stays byte-identical to the pre-field format - `clio-store` `content_envelope::tests::payload_written_before_context_existed_still_reads` - while `audit_events.detail_json` for create/update/correct is additively extended with `context_present`/`context_len`/`context_hash`, so no-context audit rows are not byte-identical)." The finding's own evidence (real CLI `clio remember "no context note" ...` -> audit row `create_memory_item | {"context_len":0,"context_present":false}`) is exactly what the new wording states.

findings.title: `retrieve`/`compose_context` do not expose stored `context` although FR-34 requires it; the deferral is documented but leaves the requirement unsatisfied
findings.evidence: `crates/clio-types/src/read.rs:119-146`: `RetrieveHit` has no `context` field and `from_item` does not carry it; `crates/clio-retrieve/src` has no context handling. Phase file §12 Known Limitations states retrieve/compose exposure is deferred to the retrieval phase.
findings.recommendation: Track the exposure in the retrieval phase and do not treat FR-34 as fully satisfied until hits carry context and any pack inclusion is budgeted under PR-1.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED for the `retrieve` read surface; pack inclusion stays out by contract. `RetrieveHit` now carries `context: Option<String>` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` (crates/clio-types/src/read.rs:145-152), populated from the stored item in `from_item` (read.rs:172); `from_belief` stays `None` (belief objects carry no context field). `compose_context` and all pack rendering are deliberately untouched, so no context enters a model-facing pack and the PR-1 budget contract is unchanged (the field's doc comment records that policy). Tests: crates/clio-types/src/read_tests.rs:97-117 `item_hit_carries_context_and_omits_key_when_absent` and crates/clio-retrieve/src/surface_tests.rs:148-174 `retrieve_tool_surfaces_context_and_omits_key_when_absent` (`assert_eq!(ctx_hit["context"], "from a team chat")`, key omitted when absent). Real CLI: `clio remember "billing retries use exponential backoff" --category tool_config --context "team chat" --bank demo --actor agent` then `clio recall "billing retries exponential backoff" --bank demo --actor agent --output json` -> `hits[0] = {'item_id': 'itm-cli-197797480-503715', 'gist': 'billing retries use exponential backoff', 'context': 'team chat'}`. Runs: `cargo test -p clio-types -p clio-retrieve --locked` -> clio-types 53 passed / clio-retrieve 149 passed, 0 failed. Phase file now states which half is live and which is deferred (see F-06).

findings.title: Requirement tool table lists `context?` for persona/task/failure/triple/belief writes; this phase implements none of them, and their reads cannot surface a stored context
findings.evidence: Requirement tool table entries `persona_put_stable(..., context?)`, `persona_observe_preference(..., context?)`, `task_upsert(..., context?)`, `failure_record(..., context?)`, `triple_add(..., context?)`, `belief_observe(..., context?)`. MCP schemas declare no `context` on those tools; only store/admit/batch/canonical_put/shared_store/correct declare it (`crates/clio-mcp/src/context_read_schema_tests.rs:141-166`). Phase file §12 documents the deferral.
findings.recommendation: Keep the documented deferral but name the owning phase explicitly and add the domain reads (persona_get, task_get/task_history, temporal_history, belief_history) to that phase's acceptance criteria.
findings.resolution: KEPT AS A DOCUMENTED DEFERRAL WITH A NAMED OWNER AND NOW A NAMED ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (the finding's recommendation, completed in r2 per the approver verdict), not implemented. The phase file's Known Limitations name Phase 100606 as the owning phase for domain-record `context?` on `persona_put_stable`, `persona_observe_preference`, `task_upsert`, `failure_record`, `triple_add`, and `belief_observe`, and the OWNING phase file now carries the criterion itself: roadmap/phase-100606-context-lifecycle-portability.md gained AC-100606-09 ('Domain-record writes accept optional `context` (persona_put_stable, persona_observe_preference, task_upsert, failure_record, triple_add, belief_observe) and the domain reads (persona_get, task_get/task_history, temporal_history, belief_history) surface the stored context per record') with test scenario T100606-13, a Task 1 required-change declaring and persisting the six domain-record `context` parameters (fail closed, never silently drop), a Task 2 required-change surfacing the stored context on the four FR-34 domain reads, and a traceability row `FR-34 / §4.4 domain records | Task 1 and Task 2 | T100606-13 | AC-100606-09`. The phase-100601 Known Limitations entry now cites AC-100606-09/T100606-13 instead of only asking for the criterion. Evidence that no caller value can be silently dropped today: the six tools' published schemas declare no `context` property (asserted by `clio-mcp/src/context_read_schema_tests.rs:141-166` for the declaring set, and the six tools are outside it), and the CLI exposes `--context` only on `remember`/`admit`/`correct` (`clio-lib/src/cli_context_tests.rs:236-239` asserts `discard` has no `--context`). Cost evidence for the deferral: persona (`persona_stable_entries`, `persona_preferences`) and beliefs (`beliefs`, `belief_confidence_entries`) have no `MemoryItem` carrier and seal per-field ciphertext columns, so each extension needs a new persisted sealed column on both backends plus trait, schema, and read changes - the storage expansion this phase deliberately avoided (its DoD records "no new SQL column").

plan_1hr: DONE (F-01) - `clio_compliance::correct` now rejects a supplied `context` on the declared continuous route with `invalid_argument` and writes nothing (crates/clio-compliance/src/correct.rs:129-143), with regression test `clio-compliance/src/correct_context_tests.rs::context_on_the_continuous_route_is_rejected_without_a_write`; real-CLI before/after output quoted in F-01's resolution.

DONE (F-02) - r1's `Forbidden` hard-fail guard was itself the defect (the KMS maps AEAD authentication failure to `Forbidden`, crates/clio-store/src/dek.rs:307): r2 removed the guard, so `inspect` keeps the metadata row and omits `context` for EVERY per-row body failure (crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs); regression test `inspect_survives_undecryptable_ciphertext_rows` pins both Forbidden sub-paths; real-CLI before/after on a tampered copy quoted in the F-02 resolution (`inspect` exit 1 forbidden -> exit 0 resilient row; `get` still reports the error). r3 corrected the phase-100601 file's two remaining descriptions (`roadmap/phase-100601-native-source-context.md:531` evidence row and `:628` Known Limitations, current numbering) that still claimed a per-row `Forbidden` error aborts `inspect`, and re-verified on the current binary: `cargo test -p clio-mcp --locked inspect_survives` -> 3 passed; tampered-copy CLI `inspect` exit 0 with the metadata row kept and no `context` key, `get` exit 1 `forbidden`.

DONE (F-03) - published `inspect` description and the in-code doc now state that the listing includes the optional source `context` for authorized readers (crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_read_defs.rs:278; verified against `clio mcp schema-export`).

DONE (F-04) - phase-file Definition of Done now scopes the no-context claim to the sealed payload (`clio-store` `content_envelope::tests::payload_written_before_context_existed_still_reads`) and states that audit `detail_json` is additively extended with `context_present`/`context_len`/`context_hash`.

DONE (F-05/F-06) - deferrals kept and owned: the retrieval half is now IMPLEMENTED (`RetrieveHit.context`, verified end to end through `clio recall --output json`), `compose_context` packs stay gist-only so the PR-1 budget is unchanged, and Phase 100606 is named as the owner of pack inclusion plus the domain-record `context?` work with the four FR-34 domain reads in its acceptance criteria.

plan_unlimited.disposition: PARTIALLY DONE - the retrieve half is implemented and verified (`RetrieveHit.context` in crates/clio-types/src/read.rs:145-152, from_item read.rs:172, key omitted when absent; clio-types `item_hit_carries_context_and_omits_key_when_absent`; clio-retrieve `retrieve_tool_surfaces_context_and_omits_key_when_absent`; real CLI `clio recall --output json` returns `context` on the hit). plan_unlimited.item: Add `context?` to persona/task/failure/triple/belief writes plus their record reads, with per-record persistence and SQLite/Postgres parity.
plan_unlimited.disposition: NOT APPLIED - deferred with the named owner rather than half-implemented. Persona and belief records have no `MemoryItem` carrier and seal per-field ciphertext columns, so a truthful implementation needs new persisted sealed columns on both backends, trait/store plumbing, published schemas, and reads; that is the storage expansion this phase deliberately avoided (its DoD records "no new SQL column") and it is now explicitly owned by Phase 100606 in the phase file. Implementing it only for the carrier-backed records (task/failure/triple) would leave the requirement half-satisfied while adding surface area, so no partial change was made.

plan_unlimited.item: Add an end-to-end legacy-data test that inspects and reads a bank containing pre-DualContent opaque rows without losing the listing.
plan_unlimited.disposition: DONE for the listing half - `clio-mcp/src/context_read_schema_tests.rs::inspect_survives_an_unreadable_legacy_row` inspects a bank holding a `put_item` opaque row together with a normal context-bearing item and asserts the listing survives with both rows and the readable row's context. Reading the opaque body itself remains an error by design (`clio-store` `open_dual` -> `content_format_mismatch`), so nothing beyond the metadata listing is claimed.

plan_unlimited.item: Add a contract test that every tool declaring a `context` parameter either persists it or rejects it, so no path can silently drop it again.
plan_unlimited.disposition: NOT APPLIED - no defect remains for it to guard, and a real version is phase-sized. The drop path is closed by F-01's fix, and the six tools that do not declare `context` cannot accept a value at all (the declaring set is pinned by clio-mcp schema tests). A genuine contract test needs a valid driver invocation per declaring tool plus a persisted-value assertion for each - the suite belongs with the Phase 100606 domain work that adds the remaining declaring tools, not in a remediation round whose coverage gate is already final.
